extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders and members of the public interested in EPA drinking-water rulemakings and related Federal Register notices (e.g., water systems, state primacy agencies, public health groups, environmental NGOs, regulated industry)
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results listing of Federal Register documents related to lead and drinking water rulemaking, notices, and regulatory reviews; contains abstracts and excerpts that state regulatory requirements, proposed standards, monitoring/reporting obligations, and program priorities. Useful for preparing comments, compliance planning, or tracking rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and Copper Rule Improvements (LCRI) — Core Revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing revisions to the National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for lead and copper informed by the LCRI, including requirements for drinking water systems to replace lead and certain galvanized service lines, removal of the lead trigger level, reduction of the lead action level to 0.010 mg/L, and strengthened tap sampling procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule also strengthens corrosion control treatment, public education and consumer awareness, requirements for small systems, and sampling in schools and child care facilities; intended to significantly reduce health impacts of lead exposure and simplify implementation relative to the 2021 LCRR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to replace lead and certain galvanized service lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems are being required to replace lead service lines and certain galvanized service lines as part of LCRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement is a central compliance obligation intended to reduce exposure; WIFIA and other funding programs are encouraged to prioritize projects that effect rapid progress on full lead service line replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead action level set to 0.010 mg/L
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is reducing the lead action level to 0.010 mg/L (10 µg/L) under the LCRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an enforceable threshold that triggers system responses under the NPDWR; the final rule replaces prior trigger-level constructs and ties actions to the new action level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of the lead trigger level
rubrics_metrics.description: The final LCRI removes the previous lead trigger level from the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal is intended to simplify the rule and shift focus to the revised action level and mandatory replacement/mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened tap sampling procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is strengthening procedures for tap sampling to improve public health protection and simplify implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes aim to improve the quality and representativeness of tap samples used to determine compliance and to reduce sampling uncertainty; details are in the rule's sampling protocol sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthened corrosion control treatment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule strengthens requirements for corrosion control treatment for water systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhanced corrosion control is intended to reduce lead release from plumbing and service lines; the rule clarifies expectations for system monitoring, optimization, and recordkeeping to demonstrate treatment effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education and consumer awareness requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule strengthens public education and consumer awareness obligations to inform customers about lead in drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements for communications (e.g., Consumer Confidence Reports, public notices) and supplemental information about lead levels and control efforts to support informed consumer decisions and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and flexibilities for small systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The LCRI includes strengthened but tailored requirements for small drinking water systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule recognizes implementation challenges for small systems and offers specific provisions to address capacity and resource constraints; small-system sampling and compliance paths are clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling in schools and child care facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule strengthens requirements for sampling in schools and child care facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures target protection of vulnerable populations (children); may require routine or targeted sampling and public disclosure of results and mitigation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Reports (CCR) — readability, supplemental lead information, and delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is revising the CCR rule to improve readability, clarity, and understandability of CCRs, require supplemental information regarding lead levels and control efforts, incorporate electronic delivery options, and improve the accuracy of information presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems serving 10,000 or more persons, CCRs must be provided biannually (twice per year). States/tribes with primacy must report compliance monitoring data (CMD) to EPA to improve oversight. Revisions are intended to improve risk communication and consumer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed perchlorate NPDWR: MCLG and candidate MCL levels and system obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed setting a perchlorate MCLG at 0.02 mg/L and is taking comment on setting an enforceable MCL at 0.02, 0.04, or 0.08 mg/L; the proposal would require monitoring for perchlorate, mitigation when levels exceed the MCL, public notification and consumer confidence reporting, and reporting to the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's analyses consider benefits and costs; although the Administrator determined benefits may not justify costs, SDWA requires issuance of a NPDWR and MCLG for perchlorate per court decision—public comments welcome on monitoring, mitigation, and notification approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: PFAS NPDWRs — MCLGs, MCLs, and hazard-index for mixtures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA finalized NPDWRs and MCLGs for six PFAS. MCLGs for PFOA and PFOS set at zero; MCLs for PFOA and PFOS promulgated at 4.0 ng/L. Individual MCLs (and MCLGs) for PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA set at 10 ng/L. For mixtures of two or more of PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and PFBS EPA finalized a Hazard Index (HI) of 1 as the MCLG and MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory approach accounts for additive toxic effects and co-occurrence; EPA estimated substantial public-health benefits (prevented deaths, illnesses) and identifies funding/technical assistance mechanisms (DWSRF, training) to support compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-Year Review candidate criteria for revising NPDWRs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Six-Year Review evaluates available information on regulated contaminants to determine if new information on health effects, treatment technologies, analytical methods, occurrence, exposure, implementation, or other factors provides a basis to support a regulatory revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review considers whether revisions would improve or strengthen public-health protection; absence of sufficient candidate contaminants may lead to no revisions at that review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory determination process (RD5) — evaluation, comment, and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: For Contaminant Candidate List regulatory determinations, EPA presents preliminary determinations and the supporting rationale and requests public comment on the process, analyses, and supporting information used to make those decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments can address the scientific, occurrence, exposure, and policy analyses underpinning decisions to regulate or not to regulate specific contaminants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited approval of alternative test procedures for contaminant analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is approving alternative testing methods for measuring contaminants in drinking water via an expedited approach to make additional methods available for compliance monitoring and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority under SDWA allows EPA to approve alternative methods; the expedited approach is intended to provide timely access to new measurement techniques, greater flexibility for labs and PWSs, reduce monitoring costs while maintaining public-health protection; details include the approved method list (93 methods in one action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lead-free pipes/fittings/fixtures — revised 'lead free' definition and compliance approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reduction of Lead in Drinking Water Act lowered the maximum lead content definition of 'lead free' from 8% to 0.25% and requires compliance based on a weighted average of wetted surfaces; some exemptions for certain plumbing products exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturers and importers must demonstrate compliance with lead-content requirements for potable-use products; rule implementing the Act (Lead Free Rule) provides calculation methods and product exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drinking Water Infrastructure Needs Survey and Assessment (DWINSA) — scope and data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducts the DWINSA (e.g., the 8th DWINSA) to estimate capital improvement needs of drinking water systems eligible for DWSRF, surveying large community water systems via census and other systems via sampling as authorized under SDWA sections 1452(h) and 1452(i)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data support capital-planning and funding decisions, inform infrastructure financing programs, and are subject to PRA/OMB review; EPA solicits public comment on information collection aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dust‑lead hazard standards and post-abatement clearance levels (DLRL/DLAL)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing lowering dust-lead hazard standards to any reportable level as analyzed by an NLLAP-recognized laboratory, renaming hazard standards to dust-lead reportable levels (DLRL) and post-abatement clearances to dust-lead action levels (DLAL), and setting post‑abatement clearance levels at 5 µg/ft2 (floors), 40 µg/ft2 (window sills), and 100 µg/ft2 (troughs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA also revises the definition of abatement so actions are based on DLALs; DLRL do not compel owners to evaluate or act unless abatement is performed or thresholds are met; public comments informed nomenclature and levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land‑disposal exemption demonstration standard (no migration to USDW)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a land-disposal restriction exemption for Class I injection wells, an applicant must demonstrate, to a reasonable degree of certainty, there will be no migration of hazardous constituents out of the injection zone or into an underground source of drinking water for at least 10,000 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstration is made under 40 CFR criteria and requires technical analysis/modeling; EPA's decision constitutes a final action with no administrative appeal for granted exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIFIA/SWIFIA NOFA priorities — project selection criteria including lead service line replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: WIFIA NOFA solicits letters of interest for credit assistance; projects should protect human health and/or the environment, improve water quality, support compliance with drinking-water standards, and WIFIA encourages projects that make rapid progress on lead service line replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFA evaluates extent to which projects serve regions with significant water-resource challenges (water quality, quantity, flood risk, regional agreements, exceptional resources) and aligns with statutory priorities and EPA initiatives.
